metrics.trucksPallets: Trucks and pallets in this schedule, with the docks and teams available shown underneath.
metrics.arrivals: When the first truck arrives and when the last one finishes unloading. The earlier the day ends, the more slack you have for late trucks.
metrics.putaway: When the last pallet leaves the staging area for the racks.
metrics.crewUtilization: The share of the teams’ working time spent unloading. A low figure means teams are often waiting for trucks or for space in staging.
metrics.late: Trucks that will finish unloading after their time window closes. The total delay in minutes is shown underneath.
metrics.bufferPeak: The most pallets in the staging area at any one time during the day. It shows how close you came to running out of space.

params.fullTruckMinutes: How long one team takes to unload a full truck. Part loads take proportionally less time.
params.fullTruckPallets: How many pallets a full truck carries. Together with the unloading time, this sets each team’s pace.
params.dockSetupMinutes: The time needed to position a vehicle at the dock before unloading starts. The team can work on another truck in the meantime.
params.bufferCapacity: The maximum number of pallets that can be held in the staging area at any one time.
params.putawayPalletsPerHour: How many pallets your forklift operators can move from staging to the racks per hour.
params.shiftChangeMinutes: How long the shift handover takes. No arrivals, unloading or putaway are planned during it.
params.breaksPerShift: How many breaks each team takes per shift. The app times them so they cause as little disruption as possible.
params.lastArrival: The latest time a truck can arrive. It leaves time to finish unloading and clear staging before closing.
params.slotMinutes: The step used for arrival and unloading times. A smaller step gives a more precise schedule but takes longer to calculate.
params.solverTimeLimitS: How long the app can spend looking for the best schedule. When time runs out, it uses the best one found so far.
params.weightTardiness: How much it matters to finish unloading within each time window. A higher value makes this goal more important.
params.weightMakespan: How much it matters to finish the day’s last unload earlier.
params.weightFlow: How much it matters to handle each truck as early as its time window allows.
params.weightBuffer: How much it matters to keep pallets in staging for as short a time as possible.

fields.windows: The time range in which the truck should arrive and be unloaded. Leave it blank if there’s no restriction.
fields.priority: When not every truck can be on time, deliveries with a higher priority are protected from delays first.
fields.hardWindow: Unloading must finish within the time window. If that’s impossible, the window is relaxed and the schedule shows a warning.

actions.import: A CSV or XLSX file with the columns numer_listu, przewoznik, data_dostawy and liczba_palet (any others are optional). Click “Check” first, then “Import”.
actions.versions: Every time you generate a schedule, it’s saved as a new version. Click a version to view it.
actions.weekStrip: Your week at a glance: trucks and schedule status for each day. The icon shows whether a schedule is ready, generating, out of date or failed.
actions.runStatus: “Optimal” means no better schedule exists. “Valid” meets every rule, but there wasn’t enough time to confirm it’s the best.

columns.arrival: When the vehicle should be at its dock — this is the time the carrier receives.
columns.unload: When unloading takes place, starting once the vehicle is in position.
columns.window: The delivery’s time window. A red “+N min” means unloading will finish late.
columns.deliveryWindow: When the truck should arrive and be unloaded. Fixed windows must be met.

welcome.title: Welcome to ETPromo!
welcome.body: In a few quick steps, we’ll show you how to load deliveries, generate a schedule and share it with your carriers.
welcome.meta: {steps, plural, one {# step} other {# short steps}} · about 2 minutes
welcome.safe: The tour won’t change any of your data.

tour.missing: You’ll see this once there’s data — for example, after a schedule has been generated.

welcome.title: Your delivery schedule in minutes
welcome.body: ETPromo gives every truck an arrival time and a dock so unloading runs smoothly. Let’s take a quick look around.

navigation.title: Three main sections
navigation.body: Load your trucks under Deliveries, describe your warehouse under Settings, then generate and share schedules on the Schedule page.

language.title: Language
language.body: Switch the app’s language here. Go ahead and try it — the tour will switch too.

import.title: Import your deliveries
import.body: The quickest way to add deliveries is from a CSV or Excel file. Choose the file, click “Check”, then “Import” once there are no errors.

addDelivery.title: Add a single delivery
addDelivery.body: Use this form for a truck that isn’t in your file. The time window and priority are optional.

deliveryList.title: Your delivery list
deliveryList.body: All upcoming trucks are listed here. Click a date to open that day’s schedule, or cancel a truck that won’t be coming.

resources.title: Describe your warehouse
resources.body: Enter your docks, teams, staging capacity, handling times and working hours. The ⓘ icon next to a field explains what it means.

weights.title: What matters most
weights.body: Priorities tell the app what to focus on, such as meeting time windows or finishing the day earlier. The defaults work well for most warehouses.

saveSettings.title: Save your changes
saveSettings.body: New settings apply the next time you generate a schedule. Existing schedules aren’t affected.

pickDay.title: Pick a day
pickDay.body: Click a day in the week overview, or use the arrows and date picker above. The icon next to each day shows its schedule status.

generate.title: Generate the schedule
generate.body: One button schedules the selected day, the other the whole week. It usually takes just a few seconds.

kpis.title: Your day at a glance
kpis.body: These tiles show the key figures: arrival times, team utilization, delays and staging occupancy. Hover over ⓘ if anything’s unclear.

arrivals.title: Arrival times
arrivals.body: This is the key table: when each truck should arrive and at which dock. A red “+N min” means that unload will finish late.

timeline.title: How the day unfolds
timeline.body: The timeline shows what each dock and team is doing throughout the day. The Staging area tab shows how many pallets are waiting to be racked.

versions.title: Schedule versions
versions.body: Each time you generate a schedule, a new version is saved, so you can compare options. Delete the ones you don’t need.

share.title: Share with your carriers
share.body: Download a PDF or use the ready-made messages in the Messages tab. You can choose the document language separately from the app language.

finish.title: You’re all set!
finish.body: You can replay this tour at any time from the Help button.

center.title: Help
center.description: Guided tour and a quick how-to.
center.contextHint: The ⓘ icon next to a field or figure explains what it means.

manual.title: User guide
manual.intro: A short guide to the app, covering the same ground as the tour, so you can read it whenever you like.

quickStart.s1: Check your warehouse settings and save them.
quickStart.s2: On the Deliveries page, load your file: “Check” first, then “Import”.
quickStart.s3: On the Schedule page, pick a day and click “Generate daily schedule”.
quickStart.s4: Review the arrival times and any late unloads.
quickStart.s5: Download the PDF or send the ready-made messages to your carriers.

whyInfeasible.q: Why can’t a schedule be generated?
whyInfeasible.a: With your current resources, not every truck fits into working hours. Move some deliveries to another day, add a team or extend working hours.

optimalVsFeasible.a: Both are fine to send. An optimal schedule is the best possible; with a valid one, there wasn’t time to confirm that.

stale.a: The day’s deliveries changed after the schedule was generated. Regenerate it before sending.

paramsChange.q: Will changing settings affect existing schedules?
paramsChange.a: No. New settings apply the next time you generate a schedule.

editDelivery.q: How do I correct a delivery?
editDelivery.a: Import a file with the same consignment note number, and the delivery will be updated.

sendEmails.a: No. You copy the ready-made message or open it in your e-mail program.
